title: ShoppingListItemRow
description: Add `CookbookApp/ShoppingLists/ShoppingListItemRow.swift` — the item row rendered inside each aisle section. Leading: tappable circular checkbox (`circle` / `checkmark.circle.fill`) calling `ShoppingList.toggle(itemAt:)`, persisted immediately. Centre: item text via SwiftUI `Text` markdown rendering, strikethrough and `.secondary` foreground when checked. Trailing: decorative `line.3.horizontal` drag handle (no gesture, no-op). Swipe-to-delete (red `.swipeActions` button, calls `removeItem(atLine:)`). Swipe-to-edit (gray button, presents `.alert` prefilled with current text; on Save calls `updateItem(atLine:newText:)`). All icon-only controls carry accessibility labels.
acceptance_criteria: Tapping the checkbox calls `ShoppingList.toggle(itemAt:)` and the mutation is persisted to disk
Checked items render with strikethrough and `.secondary` foreground colour
`line.3.horizontal` drag handle is visible but has no attached gesture (decorative only)
Right-to-left swipe reveals a red "Delete" button and a gray "Edit" button
Delete button calls `removeItem(atLine:)` with no confirmation dialog
Edit button presents `.alert` prefilled with the item's current text; Save calls `updateItem(atLine:newText:)`
Cancel on the edit alert leaves the item unchanged
Accessibility labels present on checkbox, delete, and edit actions

handoff_summary.completed: Created `CookbookApp/ShoppingLists/ShoppingListItemRow.swift` with: (1) leading checkbox button toggling between `circle`/`checkmark.circle.fill` via `onToggle` closure with accessibility label; (2) centre `Text` using `AttributedString(markdown:)` for inline markdown, with `.strikethrough` and `.secondary` foreground when checked; (3) trailing `line.3.horizontal` drag handle marked `accessibilityHidden(true)`; (4) `.swipeActions(edge: .trailing)` — red destructive Delete button (calls `onDelete`) and gray Edit button (sets `editText` and shows alert); (5) `.alert("Edit item")` prefilled with current item text, Save guard against empty input then calls `onUpdate(trimmed)`; (6) all icon-only controls have accessibility labels. Build verified successful.
handoff_summary.remaining: Downstream bead `ShoppingListDetailView` must wire up `ShoppingListItemRow` by providing closures that call `ShoppingList.toggle/removeItem/updateItem` and then persist via `ShoppingListFiles.writeText`.
handoff_summary.risks: The `onToggle`/`onDelete`/`onUpdate` closure interface is a design choice; `ShoppingListDetailView` must adopt this pattern. If that bead uses a different integration shape (e.g. `Binding<ShoppingList>`), the row interface may need adjustment — but the closure approach is idiomatic and low-risk.
handoff_summary.next_action: Tester agent should verify acceptance criteria: checkbox toggle, strikethrough styling, drag handle visibility, swipe delete/edit, edit alert prefill/save/cancel, accessibility labels.
handoff_summary.conflict_risks: No file overlap with sibling beads. `ShoppingListDetailView.swift` is a separate bead and will need to import and use `ShoppingListItemRow` — no conflict, additive only.
handoff_summary.design_decisions: Closure-based interface (`onToggle`, `onDelete`, `onUpdate`) chosen over `Binding<ShoppingList>` so the row stays stateless and the detail view owns all mutation + persistence logic. `AttributedString(markdown:)` used for item text rendering with plain-text fallback. Swipe actions use default `allowsFullSwipe` so full-swipe delete works without a confirmation dialog, matching the spec requirement.
handoff_summary.test_coverage_notes: Row is a pure view driven by closures — unit tests can verify all branches (checked/unchecked, alert cancel/save) by injecting spy closures and inspecting state transitions.
handoff_summary.known_limitations: Drag-handle reordering is decorative only (no gesture) per spec v1. `updateItem` guard against empty text is added defensively; spec does not specify this behaviour explicitly.

conflict_risks: No file overlap with sibling beads. `ShoppingListDetailView.swift` is a separate bead and will need to import and use `ShoppingListItemRow` — no conflict, additive only.

Build passes cleanly.
